unsupported.tool_callbacks: Use ScriptedTool for named tool callbacks; BashBuilder exposes lower-level custom builtins.

unsupported.cancellation: ToolExecution has no host cancellation handle; callers can drop the future or set a deadline.
unsupported.stdin: ToolRequest accepts commands and timeout_ms only; scripts can still create internal pipelines.
unsupported.tool_callbacks: BashTool accepts shell builtins, not the named tool-callback contract.
unsupported.snapshots: Each BashTool execution creates an isolated fresh Bash instance and exposes no persistent snapshot state.

unsupported.cwd: ScriptedTool intentionally uses a logic-only shell without filesystem-backed cwd configuration.
unsupported.custom_builtins: Only registered ToolDef callbacks become commands; arbitrary Bash builtins are not accepted.
unsupported.network_policy: The logic-only orchestration shell has no network builtins.
unsupported.transport_hooks: The logic-only orchestration shell has no HTTP transport.
unsupported.virtual_filesystem: Filesystem commands and redirections are intentionally rejected.
unsupported.mounts: Filesystem commands and redirections are intentionally rejected.

unsupported.cancellation: No programmatic cancellation API exists at the process boundary.
unsupported.cwd: The CLI exposes no initial virtual-cwd flag.
unsupported.env: The CLI deliberately does not inherit or expose host environment injection flags.
unsupported.custom_builtins: A standalone process cannot receive in-process host callbacks.
unsupported.tool_callbacks: A standalone process cannot receive in-process host callbacks.
unsupported.transport_hooks: The CLI exposes allow-all/default-deny policy, not a host transport callback.
unsupported.snapshots: The CLI exposes no snapshot commands.
unsupported.runtime_typescript: The CLI build does not register the TypeScript runtime.

unsupported.stdin: execute() accepts a command string and optional output callback, not top-level host stdin.

unsupported.runtime_typescript: The Python package does not compile or expose the TypeScript runtime.
